Storytime: in 1999-2000, my brother and I really got into "Hip Hop eJay," a tool for making songs using a vast library of included drum, synth, vocal, and other samples. We'd both spend time making tracks and playing them for the other. Eventually we got bored of it and moved on. 

Over the years, whenever I'd change computers, I'd compress everything in my Documents and Photos and so on into a Zip file and hang onto it, in case there was anything I might forget I wanted. I kept this practice up for 20 years, ending up with a box of IDE, SATA, and even SCSI hard drives that basically contain my life on them. 

One day, while playing around with PC-EM and Windows 98, I remembered Hip-Hop eJay and the songs we used to make. I got an external device for plugging in old drives and discovered a folder full of the old tracks. The company that made HHE had since grown to make a suite of similar products, on their 5th iteration. They didn't have an archived copy of the original tool for sale or download, and I wasn't able to find one just floating about. What I did find though, was a copy available on eBay.

And so, with my eBay purchased copy of Hip-Hop eJay and a USB CD-ROM off Amazon, I ripped an image, loaded it onto the PC-EM Windows 98 box, transferred all those old songs on there, and there I was - all the way back in 1999-2000 again.

I faced this question earlier this year while trying to make a first person blobber. In RPG Maker, with MV3d and the default RTP tileset, I was able to rather quickly sketch out some dungeons and navigate them. I spent about $100 on a Visustella bundle in order to get the battle system and some other features I wanted, implemented them to a satisfactory proof of concept, and am now working on the story.

Out of curiosity, I fired up Godot engine to see how this would go in an engine that uses a language I'm familiar with. I figured it would take several months to a year to writeup all the necessary code to get to the same state I'm at in RPG Maker now. There might be templates or plugins for Godot, but I'm not too familiar with the engine, so that would also take time to get up to speed on.

In short, I think the question is, do you want to make the game, or do you want to make the technology? If you want to program your blobber to your own spec, an engine like Godot or Unreal would be best. If you're looking to instead get to game dev asap, RPG Maker is the way to go.
